text:
support-liaison: :rotating_light: Customer report — burst of 503/504s starting ~10:12 UTC across hosted API in us-west-2. Multiple production tenants reporting failures and timeouts. Escalating to oncall. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/alerts/INC-1820
support-liaison: Summary: spike aligns with a canary rollout initiated at 10:10 (routing/traffic-split changes). Need fast triage and rollback plan.
deploy-bot: deploy-event: canary rollout `api-router@v2.13.0` -> started by devon-eng at 2024-11-06T10:10:34Z. Canary weight: 5% -> 20% automated ramping. Link: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/5542
alex-oncall: ack, I'm on it. Looking at gateway traces and error logs now.
maria-sre: seeing increased 503s on api-gateway and request timeouts from routing layer. Quick grep: `error: route_tag not found` repeated in router logs. Sample: ```2024-11-06T10:12:07Z api-router[replica-12] ERROR route-resolver: route_tag "beta-wallet" not defined, rejecting request```
alex-oncall: good catch — that would surface as HTTP 503 from the router. Any config changes that could have removed tags?
devon-eng: I pushed a routing config tweak in the canary bundle that simplified tag resolution (PR #876). It should be backward compatible but I *did* rename an internal selector key from `route_tag` -> `rt_tag` in the canary's config map. I likely forgot the compatibility shim.
beth-support: customers impacted: acme-payments, quickchat, and two internal QA tenants. Impacting tokenized billing calls — they're getting timeouts and retries.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook excerpt (routing misconfig): Step 1: Pause canary traffic or set weight=0. Step 2: Toggle feature flag `routing-compat-mode`=on. Step 3: If errors persist, rollback to previous release. Commands: ```# pause canary
redctl rollout set-weight api-router canary 0
# rollback (if needed)
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/api-router --to-revision=141
```
alex-oncall: I'm pausing the canary now. Running: `redctl rollout set-weight api-router canary 0`
alex-oncall: done — canary weight set to 0 :white_check_mark:
maria-sre: Confirmed: traffic back to stable, 503s dropping in the last 30s window. Error logs for missing `route_tag` subsided. Monitoring will be noisy until metrics stabilize.
devon-eng: ack — my change introduced the key rename. I didn't include fallback resolution path. I'll open an emergency patch to reintroduce the compatibility shim. PR incoming.
product-jamie: We need coordinated customer comms. Beth, can you notify the three impacted customers that a canary config issue caused transient 503s, we paused the rollout and traffic is stabilizing?
beth-support: I'll send a short incident note now and open tickets for refunds/credits if billing retries caused duplicate charges.
alex-oncall: maria, do you recommend a rollback or a targeted patch to the canary? Concern: rolling back may reintroduce other changes in the canary we rely on.
maria-sre: Since traffic is already on stable and errors reduced, patching the canary config and re-validating in staging is preferred. Rollback is okay if patch can't be tested quickly. For safety, keep canary at 0% until patch is validated.
devon-eng: PR #879 created with shim that accepts `rt_tag` or `route_tag`. I'll run a staging deploy and smoke tests.
ops-runbook-bot: Suggestion: run quick smoke: ```# run smoke tests
pytest tests/e2e/route_compat_test.py::test_legacy_tags -q
curl -H "x-api-key: smoke" https://api.staging.redwood.example/health
```
alex-oncall: running smoke locally against staging now.
alex-oncall: smoke tests passed. devon, can you schedule a canary re-release with the shim but increment slowly (2% -> 5%) and watch the tag-resolution metric? :eyes:
devon-eng: will do. Re-deploying canary with PR #879 now and will start at 2% weight.
beth-support: sent customer notes: short description + ETA for follow-up. Customers appreciate quick response.
product-jamie: Follow-up: add a guard in the rollout workflow to fail canary if route-resolver error rate > 0.1% in first 5 minutes. Ticket created: PROD-1122.
maria-sre: Also recommend adding a CI lint that checks for config key renames or adds compatibility shims for routing config.
devon-eng: re-deploy complete, canary at 2%. Monitoring: route-resolver error rate at 0.00% so far. Increasing to 5% in 10m if stable.
alex-oncall: monitoring shows error rate steady and latency back to baseline. I'll keep watch for 30m then close incident.
beth-support: marking impacted customers as "notified" and attaching timeline to their tickets.
support-liaison: Thanks team — great quick coordination. Postmortem owners? devon + maria to collaborate, beth to include customer impact notes. I'll open an incident doc. :thumbsup:
devon-eng: noted, will draft root cause and mitigations.
maria-sre: I'll add remediation steps to runbook and add the lint.
alex-oncall: closing our active alert after 35m of stable metrics. :lock:
beth-support: I'll update customers that the fix is validated and no further action required.
product-jamie: nice work everyone.
ops-runbook-bot: Incident closed: brief summary — misnamed routing config key in canary caused route-resolver to reject requests -> 503 spike. Canary paused, patch applied, slow ramp, monitoring passed."
